When the school district in Seattle moved its high school start time nearly an hour later in 2016, researchers who tracked students with wrist sensors found that they slept about half an hour longer on school nights, and their grades and attendance (B) [improved / deteriorated]. California went further, passing a law that took effect in 2022 requiring most public high schools to begin no earlier than 8:30. Later start times are not without costs: bus schedules, sports practices, and parents' working hours all have to be (C) [rearranged / deranged]. But the evidence suggests that the inconvenience may be a price well worth paying.

In January 2026, South Korea's Framework Act on Artificial Intelligence took effect, making the country one of the first in the world, after the European Union, to adopt a comprehensive law governing the technology. Passed by the National Assembly in December 2024, the act endeavors to reconcile two aims that often pull in opposite directions: fostering a domestic AI industry and protecting citizens from the technology's risks. It requires companies to notify users when they are interacting with generative AI and to label content, such as realistic images or video, that has been produced by it. Developers of so-called high-impact systems, used in areas such as medical care, hiring, and lending, must assess risks and explain how their systems reach decisions. Large foreign companies must also designate a local representative. Business lobbies have warned that nebulous definitions could stifle innovation, while civic organizations argue that the penalties are too modest to deter serious violations. Officials have pledged to refine the rules through detailed regulations. How rigorously the law is enforced will determine whether it becomes a model for other countries or a cautionary tale.

Conventional criminal justice asks three questions: what law was broken, who broke it, and what punishment the offender deserves. Restorative justice asks a different set: who was harmed, what do they need, and who is obliged to repair the damage. In practice, this often means bringing victims and offenders together, with the help of a trained facilitator, so that the offender hears firsthand how the crime affected the victim and takes part in deciding how to make amends. New Zealand made such meetings, known as family group conferences, a central part of its youth justice system in 1989, and similar programs have since spread to many countries. The approach is not a lenient option; confronting the person one has harmed is, for many offenders, far more daunting than sitting silently in a courtroom. Research suggests that victims who take part are generally more satisfied than those whose cases go through ordinary courts, and that reoffending often declines modestly. Restorative justice cannot replace the courts for every crime, but its central insight deserves wider attention: justice is served not only by punishing wrongdoers but by repairing what they have broken.

A dog's nose contains roughly three hundred million scent receptors, compared with about six million in a human nose, and the part of its brain devoted to analyzing smells is proportionally far larger than ours. Trained dogs can detect explosives, narcotics, and certain diseases at concentrations that laboratory instruments struggle to match. Police forces and border agencies depend on them extensively, and a well-trained detection dog can search a vehicle in minutes that would take human officers hours. Yet dogs are not infallible, and their performance hinges on training, fatigue, and, surprisingly, on their handlers. In a 2011 study, researchers placed no target scents at all in a series of rooms, but told some handlers that scents were present and marked certain spots with red paper. The dogs alerted frequently, and disproportionately at the marked locations, apparently responding to almost imperceptible cues from handlers who believed something was there. The finding does not mean that detection dogs are unreliable, but it suggests that searches should be designed so that handlers do not know in advance where, or whether, a target is hidden.

Jang Yeong-sil rose from remarkably lowly origins to become one of the most celebrated inventors of the Joseon dynasty. Born to a family of low status, he was serving as a government servant when his mechanical talent came to the attention of King Sejong, who brought him to the court and eventually granted him an official rank, an extraordinary distinction for a man of his background. His most famous creation was the Jagyeongnu, completed in 1434, an ingenious water clock that announced the time automatically. As water flowed steadily into a vessel, a rising float triggered a series of balls and levers that set small wooden figures in motion, striking a bell, a drum, and a gong at the appropriate hours. The clock spared officials the tedious chore of monitoring the water levels through the night. Jang's career ended ignominiously in 1442, when a royal palanquin built under his supervision broke, and he disappears from the records soon afterward. The clock itself did not survive intact, but a working reconstruction based on surviving descriptions was completed in 2007 and can be seen today in Seoul.

My older brother's first apartment was a single room above a noodle shop, and the day he moved in, he called to ask whether I owned a screwdriver. I did not, but our father did, and so the three of us spent a sultry Saturday assembling a bookshelf whose instructions appeared to have been garbled in translation through several languages. Father, who had crafted half the furniture in our childhood home, refused to look at the diagram. For him, assembly was a matter of ____ rather than instructions. He held each piece up to the light, grumbled, and fitted it somewhere unexpected. Twice he was mistaken, and twice he dismantled the whole thing without complaint. By evening the bookshelf stood, slightly crooked, against the only wall without a window. My brother thanked him and then, as Father was leaving, quietly asked if he could keep the toolbox for a while. Father hesitated, then relinquished it with a long litany of instructions about which screwdriver was for what. Years later, when I helped my brother move into a house of his own, the same toolbox came out of the moving truck first. Some gifts, I realized, are less about the object than about what it lets you carry on.

In 1862 Charles Darwin received a box of orchids from Madagascar, among them a striking white flower, Angraecum sesquipedale, whose nectar lay at the base of a slender tube nearly thirty centimeters long. Darwin was intrigued and made a bold prediction that rested on ____ rather than observation: since orchids depend on insects to carry their pollen, there must exist a moth with a tongue long enough to reach the nectar, and in pushing its head into the flower it would pick up pollen and carry it to the next bloom. No such moth was known, and some entomologists derided the prediction. Alfred Russel Wallace, however, defended it, noting that a kindred moth from Africa had a proboscis nearly long enough. In 1903, two decades after Darwin's death, a hawk moth from Madagascar with an enormously long tongue was formally described and christened with the subspecies name praedicta, the predicted one. Remarkably, nobody photographed the elusive moth actually feeding on the orchid in the wild until the 1990s. The story is now a textbook example of how a sound theory can anticipate discoveries that no one has yet made.

밑줄 친 낱말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
My grandfather remained <u>obdurate</u> to the end, spurning every offer to sell the orchard even after the bank's letters began arriving weekly.
obdurate 는 '고집스러운, 완고한'이라 stubborn 과 가까워요. 은행 편지가 매주 와도 과수원을 팔라는 제안을 끝까지 거절했다는 뒤 내용이 단서예요. obsequious(아첨하는)·obsolete(낡은)는 철자만 비슷한 낱말이고, contrite(뉘우치는)는 끝까지 버티는 모습과 맞지 않아요.

밑줄 친 낱말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
Exhausted after the long march, the soldiers grew <u>truculent</u>, snapping at their officers and picking quarrels over the smallest portions of bread.
truculent 는 '시비조의, 공격적인'이라 hostile 과 가까워요. 장교에게 쏘아붙이고 빵 조각 하나로 싸움을 걸었다는 뒤 내용이 단서예요. placid(차분한)·amiable(상냥한)·convivial(유쾌하게 어울리는)은 반대 방향이고, pensive(생각에 잠긴)는 싸움을 거는 모습과 맞지 않아요.

밑줄 친 낱말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
Nothing she wrote in her long letter could <u>assuage</u> the guilt he felt for having missed his brother's final days in the hospital.
assuage 는 '(죄책감·고통을) 누그러뜨리다'라 ease 와 가까워요. 형의 마지막 날들을 놓친 죄책감을 긴 편지로도 달랠 수 없었다는 문장이에요. aggravate(악화시키다)·bolster(북돋우다)는 반대 방향이고, vindicate(정당함을 입증하다)·corroborate(뒷받침하다)는 죄책감과 어울리지 않아요.

밑줄 친 낱말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
The treasurer had <u>absconded</u> with the club's savings the night before the audit, leaving behind only an empty safe and a polite note of apology.
abscond 는 '(돈을 가지고) 몰래 달아나다'라 fled 와 가까워요. 감사 전날 밤 빈 금고와 사과 쪽지만 남겼다는 내용이 단서예요. lingered(머뭇거리며 남았다)는 반대이고, abstained(삼갔다)는 앞부분 철자만 비슷하며, acquiesced(묵인했다)·capitulated(항복했다)는 돈을 들고 사라진 일과 맞지 않아요.

밑줄 친 낱말과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것을 고르시오.
The old woman asked the clerk to <u>expunge</u> her late husband's name from the list of debtors, since the loan had been repaid decades earlier.
expunge 는 '(기록에서) 지우다, 삭제하다'라 erase 와 같은 뜻이에요. 빚을 수십 년 전에 갚았으니 채무자 명단에서 이름을 빼 달라는 부탁이에요. expound(자세히 설명하다)·expedite(빨리 처리하다)는 앞부분 철자만 비슷하고, ratify(승인하다)·embellish(꾸미다)는 뜻이 달라요.

대화의 빈칸에 들어가기에 가장 알맞은 표현을 고르시오.
A: Minji, do you have a minute? It's about Friday.
B: Sure. Is this about Mr. Kang's farewell dinner?

B: Great. Does he still think we're just having an ordinary meeting that evening?
A: As far as I know. That's why I'm a little worried about Junho.
B: Junho? Why him?
A: He's hopeless at keeping secrets. Last year he told our manager about her birthday cake two whole days early.
B: Oh, I remember that. She feigned surprise, but nobody believed her for a second.
A: Exactly. And this morning I saw him chatting with Mr. Kang by the coffee machine for almost twenty minutes.
B: Did you hear what they were talking about?
A: Only the very end. Mr. Kang was laughing and saying, "Friday sounds wonderful."
B: Hmm. That could mean anything. Maybe they were talking about the weekend weather.

B: We could move the dinner to Thursday. Mr. Kang would never expect it a day early.

spill the beans 는 '비밀을 털어놓다'라는 숙어예요. 비밀을 못 지키는 준호가 강 부장과 오래 이야기했으니 깜짝 송별회를 이미 말해 버렸으면 다 망친다는 흐름이에요. break the ice(어색함을 깨다)·call it a day(일을 마치다)·hit the books(공부하다)는 비밀과 관계없고, pull one's leg(놀리다)는 깜짝 파티가 망가지는 이유가 되지 않아요.

Carved into a black stone pillar more than two meters tall, the laws of Hammurabi, who ruled Babylon in the eighteenth century BCE, are among the oldest legal codes that survive in (A) ____ form. The pillar was discovered in 1901 by French archaeologists at Susa, in present-day Iran, where it had been carted off as plunder centuries after it was made; it now stands in the Louvre. Its nearly three hundred provisions cover matters ranging from the wages of hired laborers to the punishment of builders whose houses collapsed. The code is often cited as the source of the principle of an eye for an eye, and many readers conclude that Babylonian justice was at least (B) ____, applying the same harsh rule to everyone. Yet the penalties varied markedly with the social rank of the victim: injuring a nobleman brought an equal injury in return, while injuring a commoner or a slave was often settled with a payment of silver. Scholars also debate whether the code was ever applied in actual courts. Few surviving legal records cite it, which suggests that it may have served less as a working statute than as a public (C) ____ of the king's devotion to justice.

(A) 돌기둥에 새긴 법이니 '글로 적힌(written)' 꼴로 남은 법전이에요. (B) 모두에게 같은 규칙을 적용했다(applying the same harsh rule to everyone)고 여긴다니 '공평한(impartial)'이에요. 바로 뒤 Yet 문장이 신분에 따라 벌이 달랐다고 뒤집어요. (C) 실제 재판에 거의 안 쓰였으니 왕이 정의를 중시한다는 것을 '보여 주는 것(display)'이었다는 결론이에요.

글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 낱말을 가장 알맞게 짝지은 것을 고르시오.
Hagfish are eel-shaped scavengers of the deep sea whose basic body plan has changed little over hundreds of millions of years. They lack jaws, and their skeletons are made of cartilage rather than bone, yet they are remarkably hard to (A) ____. When a shark or another predator seizes one, glands along the hagfish's body secrete a small quantity of mucus and protein threads that expand on contact with seawater into a large mass of slime within a fraction of a second. The slime clogs the attacker's gills, and underwater video recordings show predators abruptly letting go and retreating, apparently struggling to breathe. The hagfish itself avoids (B) ____ in its own defense by tying its body into a knot and sliding the knot along its length, scraping the slime away. Engineers have taken a keen interest in the threads, which are extraordinarily slender yet robust for their size. Some researchers hope to synthesize similar fibers in the laboratory as a(n) (C) ____ to the synthetic materials now made from petroleum, though no such product has yet reached ordinary shops or the wider market.

(A) 턱도 뼈도 없어 약해 보이지만(yet) 상어가 물어도 놓아 버리니 '잡아먹기(devour)' 어렵다는 말이에요. (B) 점액이 아가미를 막아 상대가 숨을 못 쉰다고 했으니 자기도 그 점액에 '숨 막히는(suffocating)' 일을 몸을 매듭지어 피해요. (C) 석유로 만든 합성 소재를 '대신할 것(alternative)'으로 실을 만들고 싶어 한다는 뜻이에요.

글의 밑줄 친 부분 가운데 어법상 옳은 것을 고르시오.
When Robert Peel founded the Metropolitan Police in London in 1829, many residents feared that a uniformed force would become an instrument of political espionage. The new officers were deliberately made to look ①<u>as different from soldiers than possible</u>: they wore blue tailcoats and tall hats instead of red uniforms, and they carried only a short wooden truncheon. The idea that the police should depend on public approval rather than on force ②<u>have been</u> associated with Peel ever since, although historians note that the famous list of nine principles bearing his name was probably compiled long after his death. Early recruits were expected to be sober, courteous, and ③<u>remarkably patient</u> with the crowds they controlled, and those who failed were summarily dismissed. A large share of the first recruits were removed from the force, many of them for ④<u>be drunk</u> on duty. Even so, the experiment proved ⑤<u>so successfully that</u> other British cities soon created similar forces of their own.

부사 remarkably 가 형용사 patient 를 꾸며 '놀랄 만큼 참을성 있는'이 되니 맞아요. 나머지는 틀렸어요. as ~ as possible 이라 than 이 아니라 as 가 와야 하고, 주어 The idea 가 단수라 has been 이어야 해요. 전치사 for 뒤에는 동명사 being drunk 가 오고, proved 뒤 보어는 형용사라 so successful that 이 맞아요.

글의 밑줄 친 문장 가운데 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.
①<u>The polygraph, often called a lie detector, does not actually detect lies.</u> It records several bodily signals at once, such as breathing, pulse, blood pressure, and the sweating of the fingertips. ②<u>The assumption behind it is that the lies a person tells cause stress, which in turn produces measurable changes in the body.</u> The trouble is that stress has many sources. ③<u>An honest suspect who is terrified of being disbelieved may react more strongly than a calm and practiced liar.</u> Critics also point out that some people can learn to manipulate their own readings. ④<u>A major report by the United States National Academy of Sciences in 2003 concluded that the scientific basis for the test, given the evidence then available, was weak.</u> For these reasons, courts in many countries refuse to admit polygraph results as evidence, although investigators still use the test as an aid in questioning. ⑤<u>Some experts argue that its real power lies in the belief of the suspect, who may confess because he considers the machine infallibly.</u>

consider 는 'consider + 목적어 + 보어' 꼴이라 보어 자리에 부사 infallibly 가 아니라 형용사 infallible 이 와야 해요(기계를 '틀림없다'고 여긴다). the lies a person tells 는 목적격 관계사가 빠진 꼴이고(the lies that a person tells), given the evidence 의 given 은 '~을 고려하면'이라는 전치사처럼 쓰는 분사라 틀려 보여도 맞아요. 비교급 more strongly than 문장, 거짓말을 직접 잡지 못한다는 문장도 맞아요.

글의 밑줄 친 부분 가운데 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.
The prisoner's dilemma, ①<u>first described</u> by mathematicians working at the RAND Corporation in 1950, is perhaps the best-known puzzle in game theory. Two suspects are arrested and held in separate rooms, ②<u>unable to communicate</u> with each other. Each is offered the same deal: betray your partner and go free, while he serves a long sentence. If both stay silent, both receive a short sentence on a minor charge; if both betray, both serve a fairly long term. Whatever the other does, each prisoner is better off ③<u>betraying</u>, so two rational players end up worse off than if they had trusted each other. The puzzle has been used to elucidate arms races, price wars, and the overfishing of shared seas. In repeated rounds, however, cooperation becomes possible. In computer tournaments ④<u>organizing</u> by the political scientist Robert Axelrod around 1980, the winning program was a simple strategy called tit for tat, ⑤<u>which began</u> by cooperating and then copied whatever the opponent had done in the previous round.

대회는 액설로드가 '연' 것이라 수동의 과거분사 organized 가 명사 tournaments 를 꾸며야 해요(by 가 단서). first described 는 '처음 설명된'이라는 수동 분사, unable to communicate 는 형용사구 분사구문, better off 뒤 betraying 은 '배신하는 편이'라는 동명사, which began 은 앞 명사를 받는 관계절이라 모두 맞아요.

글의 밑줄 친 부분 가운데 어법상 옳지 않은 것을 고르시오.
Detective fiction is a surprisingly young genre. Most historians of the form trace it to 1841, when Edgar Allan Poe published The Murders in the Rue Morgue, a story ①<u>in which</u> an eccentric amateur named C. Auguste Dupin solves a crime that has baffled the Paris police. Dupin relies not on luck or confession but on reasoning, ②<u>notice</u> small details that others overlook and drawing audacious conclusions from them. The story is told by an admiring friend who records the detective's methods, a device that Arthur Conan Doyle would later appropriate for Dr. Watson.
